decisions.reason: F1 omitted nondegeneracy, although its actual uses are on the open interval J containing r_*<a<b. Restored at least two elements and explicitly located c_0 in I_0. Compact localisation bounds the endpoint curves in J; FTC and compact-rectangle parameter differentiation give continuous partials of Phi; total differentiability and the chain rule give both endpoint terms. The Statement and proof steps are unchanged; this inaccurate general fact is nonfatal to the proof.

F5 omitted nondegeneracy, but step 1.3 applies it to (0,infinity) with a positive basepoint r_0. Restored at least two elements and r_0 in I. Signed polar integration is finite because g is bounded on each compact ball; the finite positive sphere measure yields the normalisation and uniform-continuity estimate. The radial integrand is locally continuous and bounded near zero. Splitting at r_0 supplies the primitive derivative; the first identity makes A differentiable by division by r^n>0, and product differentiation gives the second identity. Countable Choice remains explicit; n=1 is included. Statement and proof are unchanged, so this incorrect general fact is nonfatal to the actual proof.
